narrative:
Mara found Iven at the east sluice with one hand pressed to his side and the other wrapped around the gate chain. Beyond him, the rival patrol waited in the rain, their lanterns trembling gold across the black water. He had come alone, which meant either courage or a trap. Mara trusted neither.

“You’re leaking on public property,” she said.

Iven’s mouth tightened. “Then charge me for the cleaning.”

The watchmen behind her raised their crossbows. Her orders were clear: take him alive, if possible; let the sluice drown him, if necessary. His blood had stained the stones, and three of her people had died because of his last bargain. He looked at them now without apology, as though fear were another weapon he had decided not to draw.

Mara stepped between him and the bolts. “You want the gate open.”

“I want the people in the lower quarter out before your commander seals it.”

“And what do I get?”

He glanced at the knife beneath her coat, then at the iron key hanging from her belt. “A name. The one who sold your patrol’s route.”

The offer was too precise. So was the way he kept his injured side turned away from her. Mara crouched, found the wound, and shoved a folded scarf against it. Iven flinched but did not move back.

“That costs extra,” she said.

“For saving me?”

“For making me choose.”

She took the key from her belt. The watch captain swore and ordered her aside. Mara did not look at him. She told Iven he would cross first, unarmed, and leave his signet in her palm. He stared at the ring, then removed it. The metal was warm from his skin.

“If this is a trick,” she said, “I’ll use your name to hang you.”

“If it isn’t,” he answered, “you’ll still pretend you did me no favor.”

She turned the key. The sluice groaned open. Water surged through, carrying the patrol’s lantern reflections into the dark. Iven staggered toward the lower passage. Mara caught his elbow only long enough to keep him standing, then released him before either of them could mistake the gesture.

At the threshold, he looked back. “The name is Vey.”

Mara closed her fingers around the signet. “That is not an apology.”

“No,” he said. “It is what I can afford.”
title: The Price of an Open Gate
